summary: Neo Delay in Ping-pong mode with its filters open (measured: its input enters the left line only and each line's echo feeds the other): the first track's L. Length becomes Sync and Feel (or a free Time) and R. Length the right line's Offset; Feedback carries over to ±99 %; Dry thru and Wet out become a crossfade and an output gain.

rules.why: Lengths count in Length unit: ticks (the default) are Buzz's whole samples per tick, so the echo follows the tempo; a length in ticks that is a note value (1 tick = 1/16 at 4 ticks a beat, 3 ticks = 1/8 dotted, 6 = 1/4 dotted …) becomes Neo Delay's Sync and Feel, which follow the tempo too; any other length, and lengths in ms or samples, a free Time at the song's tempo and rate. R. Length becomes the right line's Offset (R ÷ L − 1, −50 … +100 %).

Both in %; each line's echo feeds the other line, as Neo Delay's Ping-pong does (measured: 2 and 3 ticks give echoes left at 2, right at 5, left at 7 ticks, each Feedback times the last); Neo Delay's stops at ±99 %.
Dry thru (on or off) and the echoes at Wet out (raw/128) add; Neo Delay crossfades them and sets the output's level: mix = wet ÷ (dry + wet), output = dry + wet.

remarks: Jeskola Cross Delay hears left + right summed (+6 dB for a centred sound, taken on the output connections so the line keeps the input's level) and, measured, feeds it into its left line only: the first echo is on the left, the next on the right, and so on: Neo Delay's Ping-pong, which sums the input to mono into its left line too. The rewritten source in the repository feeds both lines instead (a centred sound would echo on both sides at once); the binary in the package doesn't.
Each of its tracks is a pair of lines of its own (up to 8); Neo Delay has one pair: the first track's settings move, the others' are left out.
Its Max Delay attribute (1 s by default) caps its lengths; the mapping doesn't read attributes.

tolerance.measured: Windows, Neo Poly noise and chords into it, each side against its input: at its defaults (3 and 3 ticks, Feedback 50 %, Wet out 37.5 %, dry on) +0.0 dB, third octaves within 0.1 dB (chords +0.1 dB, within 0.2 dB); L. Length 2, R. Length 3 ticks, Feedback 60 %: +0.0 dB, within 0.2 dB (chords the same). Read from single bursts at 126 BPM: a centred burst echoes left at 357.1 ms (−2.5 dB), right at 714.3 ms (−8.5 dB), left at 1071.4 ms (−14.5 dB); at 2 and 3 ticks left at 238.1 ms, right at 595.2 ms (2 + 3 ticks), left at 833.3 ms (2 + 3 + 2), each Feedback times the last: Neo Delay's Ping-pong pattern
tolerance.why_not: Nothing missed at the settings measured. Not carried: its other tracks, an R. Length more than twice or under half L. Length (Offset's reach, −50 … +100 %: clamped, with a note) and its Max Delay attribute. As for Jeskola Delay, a free length lands on Time's step (0.085 %) and a long build-up reaches Neo Delay's saturator. The comparison averages each side's level over the render, so it can't see which side an echo falls on: DelayCalibration's bursts checked that.

evidence: ExternalMachines/source/buzztrax-buzzmachines/Jeskola/CrossDelay/CrossDelay.cpp (rewritten, the original source isn't available): its parameters and units; its routing differs from the binary's
ReBuzzTests/AgentReplaceTests.cs DelayCalibration (Windows): the echoes' times, sides and levels read from its input and output
